title: Pay bands
statementMd:
Label each employee's pay band: `low` below 90,000, `mid` from 90,000 up to (not including) 130,000, and `high` from 130,000. Show first name and band.

Expected columns: `first_name`, `band`.

Tables: `employees`, `departments`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: `CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END` evaluates conditions in order.
solutionMd:
```sql
SELECT first_name, CASE WHEN salary < 90000 THEN 'low' WHEN salary < 130000 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'high' END AS band FROM employees;
```
